2024 / HEALTH UX

Sy      

A health-tech concept for people who check symptoms online and need guidance that feels clear, cautious, and easy to question.

“
SymptomCheckr was designed around a stressful moment: someone wants guidance, but a confident-looking answer can make them panic or over-trust the tool.
THE THESIS

PROJECT DETAILS

ROLE
UX/UI Designer
TOOLS
Figma, AI guidance, Journey mapping, Health UX
OWNED
Guidance model, Assessment UI, Citation patterns, Saved report flow

Problem, decision, evidence

The product choice and the proof available today.
View Live Demo

Problem

01
Symptom guidance can make people more anxious when it does not show confidence, sources, or limits.

Decision

02
Show confidence levels, source links, and plain-language reasoning instead of hiding the logic behind a simple answer.

Shipped proof

03
Designed a calmer AI-assisted flow with confidence levels, citations, and saved reports for follow-up care.

Evidence-aware audience model

Audience assumptions to validate
This model connects the available project evidence to a workflow that still needs direct research.

AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS

Person checking symptoms who needs clarity without a fake diagnosis.

They may be anxious, overloaded, or trying to decide whether their next step should be self-care, telehealth, or urgent support.

WORKING NEED
A cautious AI-assisted flow with confidence levels, sources, and saved reports for follow-up care.
RISK TO TEST
Health guidance can create more anxiety when it hides uncertainty or presents a single answer without context.

EVIDENCE BOUNDARY

The available project archive does not preserve participant counts, interview notes, or a research synthesis for this audience model. Treat it as a design hypothesis to test, not a measured persona.

WHAT THE SOURCES SUPPORT

The project archive supports the problem framing, intended workflow, and interface evidence shown in this case study. It does not establish how common these behaviors are across the broader audience.

The portfolio record identifies my role as UX/UI Designer. The available archive does not preserve enough collaborator detail to attribute specific decisions beyond that role.

WORKFLOW TO VALIDATE

01
Describe symptoms

Enter the current concern in a guided flow that keeps the language plain and calm.

02
Review confidence

See the likely direction and uncertainty instead of a sealed black-box answer.

03
Check sources

Use citations and reasoning cues to decide how much weight to give the guidance.

04
Save next steps

Keep the report and follow-up path available if clinical care or telehealth is needed.

Which step creates enough value for them to continue or retu

A security monitoring dashboard that turns third-party script risk into readable scans, risk visuals, and AI-generated code fixes.

Vault.js Validate was a security dashboard sprint built around alert fatigue: teams get warnings all day, but still need to know what to fix first.
THE THESIS

PROJECT DETAILS

ROLE
UX/UI Designer and Frontend Developer
TOOLS
React, Tailwind CSS, AI UX, Security visualization
OWNED
Risk dashboard, Remediation flow, Visual identity, Frontend prototype

Problem, decision, evidence

The product choice and the proof available today.

Problem

01
Security teams needed to know which third-party scripts mattered and what to fix first.

Decision

02
I designed and built Vault.js Validate around a security analyst's next action: scan the attack surface, see vendor relationships, read the risk in plain English, and apply or review an AI-generated fix.

Shipped proof

03
Created a dashboard concept that turns attack-surface scanning into plain-English risk and remediation steps.

Evidence-aware audience model

Security analyst triaging third-party script risk.

Interactive storytelling apps often felt repetitive and thin, especially around diverse character depth.

02
Created a platform concept that prioritized authentic storytelling through diverse creator collaboration, quality character development, and user-centric design that put narrative experience first.

The product choice and the proof available today.

Fragrance discovery is expensive, opaque, and hard to translate from taste into actual products.

Decision

02
ScentStack addresses these gaps through three integrated features: (1) Discover—a comprehensive dupe database showing luxury fragrances alongside affordable alternatives with 90% average savings, (2) Layering Lab—computer vision technology that analyzes your existing fragrances and suggests complementary combinations, and (3) Dream Lab—GPT-5 powered natural language processing that translates scent descriptions into concrete fragrance recommendations.

Shipped proof

Built a consumer product with 1700+ dupes, dream-scent matching, and photo-based layering recommendations.

Fragrance shopper translating taste into affordable or layerable options.

Dupe research lives across forums and reviews, while layering advice assumes insider knowledge.

A client wanted to prove a music app could feel calm and focused instead of becoming another social feed.

Decision

02
A clean, responsive music streaming MVP that prioritizes the music experience over everything else - no social feeds, no complex menus, just good tunes.

Built a responsive MVP that kept the listening experience simple enough for validation and user testing.
